summary: Daily run 2026-10-28, window Oct 24-27 (full 4 days; the unmodified step-1 query timed out once and ran on the identical re-send, no narrowing). Step 1: 40 flags with >=3 keys spiking. Dropped as artifacts, not attacks: cdn-header-order-only-have-single-cookie (49 keys, ~5.8M/day) was created 2026-10-24 04:30 (c.koay, ticket 140244), baseline 0. country-timezone-mismatch (56 keys) is not edited (2023), but it steps from ~31k to ~84k sampled/day on every key at once on Oct 25, the day EU DST ended (US ends Nov 1). That is a calendar/timezone-table artifact; the same step will distort tz-mismatch flags until ~Nov 1. g-ip-connection-type-velocity-short-term-abuse-wired-1point5x/2x/3x: rule rewritten Oct 21 (key_a/key_b -> key/value), 0 before Oct 21, so 3 of 7 baseline days are ~0 (same call as the Oct 22 run). Spike-scan TT names created Oct 19-20 (g-cdn-ends-cl-rfc-ct-before-cl-tz-mismatch-grease 5 keys, g-rfc-ct-before-cl-device-param-spoofing-di-dict3-st-1x 3 keys): still treated as artifacts, because their names entered TELLTALE_LIST from zero inside the Oct 17-23 baseline. Duplicates: ja4-dict-1-challenger-is-supicious-not-included (= ja4-dict-1-challenger) and sus-flag-cdn-header-order-has-sec-fetch-user (= g-cdn-header-order-has-sec-fetch-user). Kept with a caveat: g-di-dict-7 1x/4x and g-di-dict-15 4x were edited 2026-10-27 03:36-04:02 (m.davies; 1x changed from threshold_breached to short_term_threshold_ratio >= 3). That is stricter and their baseline is not ~0, so the window spikes are not caused by the edit, but Oct 27 counts are on the new definition. Top surviving single flags: g-di-dict-7 1x on 8 keys (Amazon IDS K2 ~83k/day vs 14k, gtop100 66k vs 11k, Highlight AI Chat 54k vs 1k, BofA Beacon ATM 22k vs 0, Airbnb Account Lookup 11k vs 0); g-di-high-risk-signature-2x-LT on 7 (BofA Beacon ATM 137k vs 0, Microsoft Identity Signup 131k vs 36k, Amazon IDS 45k, Tinder PreSMS 39k, DoorDash 20k); ja4-dict-1-challenger on 7 (Pinterest Login 156k vs 2k, Pinterest Reg 19k, AT&T Login 8k, Dropbox, Airbnb, Pinterest Challenge, Figma); bba is-signature 0..1-1..0 on 6 and g-biometric-mouse-sampling-inconsistency on 5 (Adobe Sign Up, Amazon IDS, Microsoft Signup); cdn-header-order-contains-pragma (Amazon IDS 117k vs 24k); client-hints-mobile-ua-not-mobile (Roblox Signup ~1.05M vs 280k); g-cdn-header-order-has-sec-fetch-user and g-ip-velocity-long-term-abuse-2x (Uber SMS 756k and 414k/day). Step 2 (16-flag vocab in the session scratchpad, arity <= 4, limit 20): 12 surviving step-1 flags + g-device-parameter-spoofing, g-page-level-biometrics-empty-or-null, g-di-dict-3 1x and client-hints-has-not-a-brand-grease. The 16-flag cap left out the other tracked-combo flags (rfc ct-before-cl, ends-with-cl/te, tz no-vpn, single-click, rta-isp, high-risk-sig-st, webgl, appleos, sec-fetch-dest, os-spoofing). Only one combo reached keys_spiking >= 5 and spike_share >= 0.5: ja4-dict-1-challenger + di-short-count-300-fp-pixel-ratio-1 (8 keys, share 0.91). It is a subset of live dishort300_dp_spoof_ja4_dict1, but on most keys it fires without g-device-parameter-spoofing (exact Oct 24-27: Roblox Signup K2 231k, 77% verified, 4% with dp-spoof; Pinterest Login 224k, 99% verified; Roblox Login 36k, 3% verified; gtop100 34k, 66% verified, 98% = live triple; Pinterest Reg 30k, 99% verified; Airbnb Account Lookup 9.2k, 70% verified; Wells Fargo Login 8.7k, 52% verified; Adobe ARP FF 7.4k, 16% verified). Not proposed: the pair appears from 0 on 5 unrelated keys at the same hour (Oct 27 ~06 UTC). On Pinterest Login ja4-dict-1 went from ~0.2% to ~62% of traffic with flat volume. That points to an upstream JA4 dictionary or client change. Roblox Signup was a one-day Oct 24 burst at 78% verified. Watch Roblox Login (36k, 3% verified, started Oct 27) and Adobe ARP FF. Every other combo with >= 5 keys had share <= 0.38 (dict-7 + grease/dp-spoof/pagebio 0.29-0.38 on Amazon IDS, gtop100, Highlight AI, BofA ATM, Microsoft Signup, Airbnb, Blizzard ROW Login, CTM UK; sec-ch-ua upcoming-chrome + grease 0.30; pragma + grease 0.13; ja4 + pagebio 0.04), so they are not attack-specific. No new candidates; no drafts validated; combos.json unchanged.
